facts.statement: The genus name Grallistrix means 'owl on stilts' because of their long legs and terrestrial habits evolved without mammalian predators.
facts.quote: The genus received this name due to the long legs and terrestrial habits which they evolved in the absence of mammalian predators on their island homes.

facts.statement: These owls fed on smaller birds, including Hawaiian honeycreepers.
facts.quote: They fed on smaller birds such as Hawaiian honeycreepers.

facts.statement: Although capable of flight, these owls likely hunted mostly on the ground to fill niches occupied by medium-sized predatory mammals.
facts.quote: They were also able to fly, but likely did most of their hunting on the ground, filling the niches occupied by medium-sized predatory mammals elsewhere.

facts.statement: Scientists have never seen these owls alive; they are known only from subfossil bones.
facts.quote: The owls were never seen alive by scientists and are known only from subfossil bones.

facts.statement: The genus Grallistrix was described by Olson and James in 1991.
Grallistrix lived from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, between 0.129 and 0 million years ago.

The type species of the genus Grallistrix is Grallistrix auceps.
